title: Luigi Galvani (1791) De Viribus Electricitatis in Motu Musculari Commentarius — Original Copperplate Engravings (Tab. I–IV), Subsequent Electrophysiology Plates (Aldini, Matteucci, Ure), & Quantitative Current-to-Twitch Laws

title_page_1791.description: 1791 Bologna title page: ALOYSII GALVANI DE VIRIBUS ELECTRICITATIS IN MOTU MUSCULARI COMMENTARIUS (Bononiae, Ex Typographia Instituti Scientiarum, 1791).

pars_prima_page_363.description: Opening page (Opuscula p. 363, Pars Prima: De viribus electricitatis artificialis in motu musculari).

tabula_I_artificial_electricity.description: Tabula I (Pars Prima, 1780-1786): Electrostatic friction machine (Fig. 1), prepared frog on table (Fig. 2) and enlarged frog preparation (Fig. 4, labels C, D, F, G, M), flask on side pedestal (Fig. 3), Leyden jars (Figs. 5-6), and overhead wire ('filo ferreo').

tabula_I_cropped_lab.description: Cropped high-contrast detail of Tabula I (Tom. VII, Pag. 418, Tab. 1) showing the electrostatic friction wheel (Fig. 1), prepared frog (Fig. 4), and Leyden jars (Figs. 5-6).
tabula_I_cropped_lab.license: Public Domain (Wikimedia Commons File:Luigi Galvani Experiment.jpeg)

tabula_II_atmospheric_electricity.description: Tabula II (Pars Secunda, 1786): Atmospheric electricity experiment on the terrace of Casa Galvani in Bologna. Insulated lightning-rod wire (A-B) connected to prepared frog crural nerves on the courtyard table, grounded via a wire into the courtyard water well, plus the right-hand niche showing a frog suspended on an iron grating in serene weather.

tabula_III_bimetallic_arcs.description: Tabula III (Pars Tertia, Sept 1786): Discovery of metallic arcs (Figs. 9-16, with Figs. 15-16 in the top-left inset; engraved by J. Zambelli). Bimetallic and monometallic conducting arcs bridging the exposed spinal cord/crural nerve plexus and gastrocnemius muscle.

tabula_IV_animal_electricity_circuits.description: Tabula IV (Pars Tertia & Quarta, 1791, Figs. 17-21): Fig. 17 frog on tilted board; Fig. 18 frog on board (E, F, G); Fig. 19 frog bridging twin water-filled glass vessels (A, B) with conducting arc (C, D); Fig. 20 seated experimenter dissecting warm-blooded mammal (lamb) sciatic nerve; Fig. 21 two experimenters forming a human-chain circuit.

wellcome_sciatic_nerve_detail.description: Wellcome M0012614 ('Tav. I', Figs. 1-4 from the 1792 Modena / 1794 Italian edition): Isolated frog sciatic-gastrocnemius nerve-muscle preparations showing spinal nerves (H, I), feet (G, M), and single vs. dual bimetallic arcs joined at s.

wellcome_frog_preparation_fig3.description: Wellcome L0002011 ('Frog preparation according to Galvani', Figs. 2-14): Iconic anatomical engraving (Fig. 3) of the isolated frog vertebral column, bilateral crural nerves, iliofibularis/gastrocnemius musculature, and webbed hindfeet used for computer-vision segmentation and articulated kinematic warping.

galvanoscopic_frog_detector.description: Wellcome L0011450 ('Fig. 8. The Galvanoscopic Frog', Matteucci 1838-1842): Isolated frog leg inside an insulating glass tube with protruding sciatic nerve lead, used as an ultra-sensitive microampere biological current detector (~1.8 uA threshold at 2.5 ms).

aldini_metal_free_nerve_muscle_loop.description: Wellcome L0001964 (Giovanni Aldini 1794/1803, 'Fig. 3'): Direct hand-held contact between the frog's crural nerve and injured/intact gastrocnemius muscle surface without any metal, proving intrinsic animal electricity (42 mV demarcation injury potential driving 3.4 uA).

matteucci_series_frog_battery.description: Carlo Matteucci (1842-1845) 'Frog Battery' (Pile de grenouilles, top-left), bell-jar apparatus (top-right), and 3-leg 'Induced Secondary Contraction' cascade (bottom) where the action current of Muscle 1 stimulates the nerve of Leg 2 and Leg 3.

ure_1818_clydesdale_voltaic_trough.description: Louis Figuier 'Les Merveilles de la Science' Fig. 333 ('Le docteur Ure galvanisant le corps de l'assassin Clydsdale'): Dr. Andrew Ure's 4 Nov 1818 Glasgow demonstration applying a 270-plate Voltaic trough battery to the spinal and phrenic/sciatic nerves (following Aldini's 1803 London demonstration), illustrating high-current multi-plate Voltaic tetanus.

hindlimb_anatomy.source: Ecker & Gaupp, Anatomie des Frosches (1896-1904); rest-pose landmarks on Wellcome L0002011 Fig. 3

insect_comparative_parameters.provenance_note: Illustrative comparative model parameters based on Hoyle (1955) Proc. R. Soc. B, Usherwood (1962), Jan & Jan (1976) J. Physiol., Burrows (1996), and Dickinson et al. (1999) Science. Whereas frog gastrocnemius grades force by recruiting ~300 ACh/Na+ motor units (1.8-15 uA), insect tibial extensor muscles use 2 excitatory glutamatergic axons (SETi slow frequency-graded, FETi fast ballistic) + 1 GABA common inhibitor (CI).

current_to_twitch_experiments.apparatus: Homogeneous single metal probe (pure Fe or pure Cu)
Frog leg in glass tube with sciatic nerve lead at liminal threshold
current_to_twitch_experiments.regime: Liminal Threshold (Pfluger Stage I: Make Only)

current_to_twitch_experiments.apparatus: Sciatic nerve bridging injured/cut and intact gastrocnemius surface (zero metals)
current_to_twitch_experiments.regime: Pfluger Stage I Weak Current (Cathodal Make Only)

current_to_twitch_experiments.apparatus: 5 cut frog thighs wired in series (5 x 42 mV = 210 mV, R_tot = 22.8 kOhm)
current_to_twitch_experiments.regime: Graded Recruitment (Onset of Pfluger Stage II)

current_to_twitch_experiments.apparatus: Brass spinal hook + Iron railing/plate (Fe/Cu bimetallic arc, 35x threshold)
current_to_twitch_experiments.regime: Pfluger Stage II Medium Current (Make AND Break Twitches!)

current_to_twitch_experiments.apparatus: Silver-Zinc arc bridging crural nerve and gastrocnemius (69x threshold)
current_to_twitch_experiments.regime: Supramaximal Pfluger Stage II (Double Twitch: Make + Break)

current_to_twitch_experiments.apparatus: 12-cell Voltaic pile (13.2 V, R_tot = 20.3 kOhm) ascending (Anode near muscle)
current_to_twitch_experiments.regime: Pfluger Stage III Anodal Block! (0% Make -> 100% Violent Break)

current_to_twitch_experiments.investigator: Ure (1818) / Du Bois-Reymond & Helmholtz (1850) 40 Hz Tetanus
current_to_twitch_experiments.apparatus: Voltaic trough / Du Bois-Reymond inductorium (40 Hz repetitive train, 25 ms spacing)
current_to_twitch_experiments.regime: Fused Tetanic Contraction (3.75x Single-Twitch Force = 4.50 N!)
